The candidate correctly identifies onset_seconds as high-information and separately predicts lte 2, but the source observation itself is an upper-bound statement ('within 2 seconds') while /observations/0/qualifiers/onset_seconds stores only the bare scalar 2. The work package does not define whether that scalar means an exact onset or an upper bound, so faithfulness of the stored high-information qualifier cannot be established without guessing. The distinction could affect permitted timing conclusions.

The source establishes onset at no more than 2 seconds. The hypothesis prediction explicitly preserves that relation with operator lte and value 2, but the observation-level timing is represented as onset_seconds: 2 without an operator. Because the package supplies no semantics establishing that this observation field denotes an upper bound rather than an exact value, the observation-level timing representation is uncertain.
Both cases are represented with dose_units 10, and the modifier claim correctly records that the represented 10-unit dose is held constant across the comparison.

The source route is intravenous and the form is liquid for the positive exposure and the same intravenous-liquid exposure for the control; those route and form values are preserved in both observations.
